problem_text:
A logistics firm must dispatch a single vehicle to perform maintenance at eight distinct facilities, whose grid positions on a company map are specified as follows:

Facility Alpha: Grid reference (127,162)  
Facility Beta: Grid reference (171,51)  
Facility Gamma: Grid reference (138,156)  
Facility Delta: Grid reference (56,2)  
Facility Epsilon: Grid reference (87,180)  
Facility Zeta: Grid reference (191,81)  
Facility Eta: Grid reference (82,9)  
Facility Theta: Grid reference (134,37)

The travel distances along permitted routes, measured in kilometers, are precisely known:

Alpha to Gamma: 12.5 km  
Alpha to Delta: 175.0 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 43.9 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 103.2 km  
Alpha to Eta: 159.5 km  
Alpha to Theta: 125.2 km  
Beta to Gamma: 110.1 km  
Beta to Delta: 125.0 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 153.9 km  
Beta to Zeta: 36.1 km  
Beta to Eta: 98.4 km  
Beta to Theta: 39.6 km  
Gamma to Delta: 174.5 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 56.4 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 91.8 km  
Gamma to Eta: 157.3 km  
Gamma to Theta: 119.1 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 180.7 km  
Delta to Zeta: 156.4 km  
Delta to Eta: 26.9 km  
Delta to Theta: 85.5 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 143.6 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 171.1 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 150.5 km  
Zeta to Eta: 130.6 km  
Zeta to Theta: 72.0 km  
Eta to Theta: 59.1 km

Direct travel between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta is not possible due to an access restriction. Furthermore, due to a scheduling mandate, the final route must incorporate exactly one—and not both—of the following two critical links: the connection between Beta and Gamma, or the connection between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a circuit that visits every facility exactly once, commencing and concluding at the same starting point.
